Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: Viktor Bunyakovsky. It is considered one of the most important and widely used inequalities in mathematics.
Who is credited with discovering Phosphorus?
Phosphorus: Hennig Brand. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Formed by the angle of thyroid cartilage around the voice box, this neck protrusion becomes a prominent secondary sex characteristic in most men during puberty — what is it commonly called?
Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
This emotion is defined by dread over events that haven't happened yet, distinguishing it from fear, which responds to a threat that's already present. What is it?
Anxiety is an emotion characterized by an unpleasant state of inner turmoil and includes feelings of dread over anticipated events.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered in 1962 while still a Cambridge Ph.D. student — then later turned, controversially, to Transcendental Meditation. Which physicist is he?
Brian Josephson (born 4 January 1940) is a British theoretical physicist and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge.
Bordered by Aquila, Sagittarius, and Aquarius in the sky's watery region, this half-goat, half-fish zodiac figure is the tiniest of the twelve — which constellation?
Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.

This interdisciplinary field, whose name combines a Latin word for 'accusation' with a Greek suffix meaning 'study of,' draws on sociology, psychology, economics, and law to examine crime and deviant behavior. What field is this?
Criminology (from Latin crimen, 'accusation', and Ancient Greek -, -logia, from logos, 'word, reason') is the interdisciplinary study of crime and deviant behaviour.
This annual herb in the celery family, native to North Africa and West Asia, is grown across Eurasia for both its feathery leaves and its seeds, both used to flavor food — what herb is it?
Dill (Anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family Apiaceae.

Distinguished by permanently erect front fangs and a habit of rearing up while flaring a neck flap, which family of mostly venomous snakes ranges from an 18 cm white-lipped species to a nearly 6-metre giant?
Elapidae (commonly known as elapids, from Ancient) is a family of snakes characterized by their permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth.

This genus of 700-plus flowering trees gets its name from Greek words meaning 'well covered' — a nod to the little cap fused over its stamens — and most species are native to Australia. The leafy 'gum trees' in question are which?
Eucalyptus is a genus of more than 700 species of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
Found at the terminal end of the limb in many vertebrates, this weight-bearing anatomical structure enables locomotion and is typically made up of multiple bony segments — what is it?
Foot (pl.: feet) is an anatomical structure found in many vertebrates. The plural form feet is an instance of i-mutation.

Sometimes called the 'lesser apes' to distinguish them from chimpanzees, gorillas, and orangutans, these smaller, tailless primates live in forests from eastern Bangladesh through Southeast Asia and don't build nests — what are they?
Gibbon are apes in the family Hylobatidae (hylobatids).
This flatfish's English name blends words for 'holy' and 'flat fish,' a nod to its place on the Catholic holy-day menu. Which bottom-dwelling fish?
Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
Nesting monogamously in tree cavities across Africa, Asia, and Melanesia, these birds are unique for having their first two neck vertebrae fused solid — which birds?
Hornbill are birds found in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Melanesia of the family Bucerotidae.

Co-creator of the breakthrough neural network AlexNet and a contributor to landmark AI systems including GPT and AlphaGo, this computer scientist has won a major deep-learning research award three years running — who is he?
Ilya Sutskever (born 1986) is a computer scientist who specializes in machine learning.
This American psychiatrist and Communist Party USA member is best remembered today for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer — who was she?
Jean Tatlock (February 21, 1914 - January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
Drawing on physiology, biomechanics, and neuropsychology, this scientific discipline studies human body movement and underpins fields from sports psychology to physical therapy — what is it?
Kinesiology (from Ancient Greek (knsis) 'movement' and - -loga 'study of') is the scientific study of human body movement.
This German-born American businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, launching his San Francisco firm in 1853 — who is he?
Levi Strauss (STROWSS; born Lb Strau,; February 26, 1829 - September 26, 1902) was a German-born American businessman who founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.
Touch this creeping legume's compound leaves and they fold inward within seconds, only reopening minutes later — a textbook example of rapid plant movement. What plant is it?

Mimosa pudica (also called sensitive plant, sleepy grass, sleepy plant, action plant, humble plant, touch-me-not, touch-and-die, shame plant or shy plant) is a creeping annual or perennial flowering plant of the pea/legume family Fabaceae.
Developed under a hypersonic flight program in the late 1990s, three single-use examples of this scramjet aircraft were built, the first destroyed in a 2001 test flight — which record holder is it?
NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Built from proteins, DNA, and RNA around specific chromosomal regions, this nuclear structure is being studied as a target for cancer chemotherapy — what is it?
Nucleolus (pl.: nucleoli) is the largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
Founded as a science by Georges Cuvier in 1796, when he demonstrated evidence for extinction, this field studies prehistoric life mainly through fossils — what's the discipline?
Paleontology is the scientific study of the life of the past, mainly but not exclusively through the study of fossils.
Which management theorist and educator's writings on organizing business, government, and nonprofit sectors made him one of the most influential thinkers on modern management?

Peter Drucker (November 19, 1909 - November 11, 2005) was an Austrian American management consultant, educator, and author, whose writings contributed to the philosophical and practical foundations of modern management theory.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.

This bird of prey now breeds only in Europe, though it once also ranged across West Asia and Northwest Africa, with northern populations historically wintering as far as western Africa — what bird is it?
Red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
This root vegetable — a hybrid of cabbage and a related turnip-like plant — goes by different names in North America and Britain, and is often confused for a big turnip. What is it?
Rutabaga (North American English) or swede (British English and some Commonwealth English) is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus (which also includes rapeseed).
This Soviet rocket engineer led the early development of his country's space program and designed the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile — who is he?
Sergei Korolev was Soviet aerospace engineer (1907–1966).

Barred from a formal education, she learned mathematics from her father's library and wrote to Gauss under the male pseudonym 'Monsieur Le Blanc,' later winning a Paris Academy prize for her work on elasticity. Which French mathematician was she?
Sophie Germain (1 April 1776 - 27 June 1831) was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
Developed from an earlier design, this variable-sweep-wing Soviet fighter-bomber served from 1967 to 1990 and was exported in variants like the Su-22 — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-17 (NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Its wild form is dioecious while domesticated versions bear hermaphrodite flowers — this Mediterranean-native plant is the ancestor of nearly all wine and table varieties — what species?

Vitis vinifera is a species of flowering plant, native to the Mediterranean region, Central Europe, and southwestern Asia, from Morocco and Portugal north to southern Germany and east to northern Iran.
Which East Asian citrus fruit, believed to have originated in central China as a hybrid of mandarin orange and ichang papeda, is now also grown in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe?
Yuzu (Citrus junos, from Japanese or) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
Nicknamed the 'upside-down tree' for its unusual silhouette, this genus of long-lived African and Malagasy giants was named after a French naturalist — what genus is it?
Adansonia: Genus of trees known as baobab.
Made in the adrenal cortex, this hormone tells the kidney to hang onto sodium and dump potassium, quietly steering your blood pressure and blood volume — what is it?
Formed when ammonia gains an extra hydrogen ion, this positively charged molecule, NH4+, is a key player in the global nitrogen cycle — what is it?
This scientific practice of systematically measuring the human body has been used in paleoanthropology, historical living-standards research, and modern clothing design — what is it called?
Anthropometry: Measurement of the human individual.

This umbrella term for joint disease covers conditions like osteoarthritis, most common in weight-bearing joints as people age, and the autoimmune form that typically targets the hands and feet. What condition is this?
This Indian jurist studied economics at Columbia and the London School of Economics before becoming the chief architect of his country's constitution. Who was he?
B. R. Ambedkar: Indian jurist, economist, politician and social reformer (1891–1956)
Strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and currants all fall under this small, pulpy, often brightly colored category of fruit — which Britain calls "soft fruit." What is it?
Berry: In the culinary sense, small edible fruit.
Launched in 1993 as a redesigned-wing, glass-cockpit upgrade of an earlier narrow-body jetliner series, this aircraft competes chiefly against the Airbus A320 family — which aircraft is it?
Boeing 737 Next Generation: Single-aisle airliner family.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways typically causes a cough lasting around three weeks and is usually caused by a virus?
Bronchitis: Inflammation of the large airways in the lungs.
Originally defined as the heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius, this unit of energy in nutrition actually refers to a kilocalorie — what is it?

Calorie: Unit of energy used in nutrition. The small calorie or gram calorie is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius (or one kelvin).
Blending science, aesthetics, and technique, this discipline wrestles with projecting a round world onto flat media while deciding what details to keep or cut — what is it called?
Cartography: Study and practice of making maps.
Holder of 186 patents, this American engineer ran research at General Motors for nearly three decades and gave the world the electric car starter, leaded gasoline, and Freon — who was he?
Charles F. Kettering: American inventor, engineer and businessman (1876–1958)
Despite its common 'cat' nickname, this small nocturnal mammal from Africa and Asia is not a feline at all — and one African species yields a musky scent long used in perfumery — what is it?
Civet: Mammals of the families Viverridae and Nandiniidae and the genus Fossa.
Greenish-brown above and off-white below, this migratory leaf warbler is named onomatopoeically for its simple two-note song — which bird?
Common chiffchaff: Small migratory passerine bird found in Europe, Asia and north Africa.
Which tart fruit ripens on trailing evergreen vines with dark pink flowers, turning from light green to red as it matures?
Cranberry: Group of plant species bearing edible fruit.
Originally developed as an antidepressant, this fast-acting SSRI was later approved to treat premature ejaculation and was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2003 — what drug is it?
Dapoxetine: Medication used to treat premature ejaculation.
Marketed as Lanoxin, this centuries-old heart medication boosts contraction strength while slowing the heart rate, but can cause blurred vision and breast enlargement in excess — what is it?
Marked by itchy 1-2mm blisters on the palms and soles that clear in three to four weeks but often return, this form of dermatitis has no known cause — what is it?
Dyshidrosis: Inflammatory disease of the skin in humans.

Often tangled up with mood, temperament, and creativity, these neurophysiological states carry a degree of pleasure or displeasure — yet scientists still can't agree on a single definition. What are they?
Dubbed the 'father of geometry,' this ancient Greek mathematician's treatise Elements dominated the field for nearly two thousand years — who is he?
Found on birds and even some non-avian dinosaurs, this complex evolutionary structure aids flight, insulation and waterproofing, and gives its name to the study of plumology — what is it?
Also called vitamin B9, this essential nutrient the body can't make itself is vital for building DNA and RNA — which is why its synthetic form, folic acid, is added to fortified foods. What is it?
Folate: Vitamin B9; nutrient essential for DNA synthesis. Folate, also known as vitamin B9 and folacin, is one of the B vitamins.
Sometimes called 'poor man's pepper' or 'pepper grass,' this fast-growing herb has a peppery bite similar to mustard — which plant?
Garden cress: Species of edible herb.
Nicknamed the "silent thief of sight" because it steals vision slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma: Group of eye diseases related to poor retinal and nerve perfusion.
Known to the British as the Martlet, this American carrier-based fighter entered service in 1940 and remained the U.S. Navy's best fighter against the Mitsubishi Zero until mid-1943 — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat: United States Navy World War II era fighter plane.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

In this heart condition, the muscle walls, especially the wall between the ventricles, thicken without an obvious cause, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes disrupting its electrical signals — which condition?

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Enlargement of the heart muscle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.
Practitioners of this medical specialty are called internists in North America but simply 'physicians' in Britain, and often juggle patients with complex, multi-system disease — what field is it?
Internal medicine: Medical specialty dealing with adult diseases.
He won the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly half a century later, the very first Abel Prize in 2003 — which French mathematician of algebraic topology and geometry is it?

Conceived as a high-speed 'Schnellbomber' for the German Luftwaffe, this twin-engined WWII aircraft evolved into everything from a night fighter to the explosive lower half of composite 'Mistel' combinations — what is it?
Junkers Ju 88: German twin-engined multirole combat aircraft.
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?

This Canadian physicist worked on the Manhattan Project determining critical mass values for uranium and plutonium, and in 1946 was fatally exposed to radiation in a lab accident at Los Alamos — who is he?
Louis Slotin: Canadian physicist and chemist (1910–1946)
In larger organizations it stacks into a pyramid, with a board and CEO at the top setting strategy — the broad practice of administering a business or government. What is it?
Management: Coordinating the efforts of persons.
Home to the heart, esophagus, trachea, thymus, and central chest lymph nodes, this compartment of the thoracic cavity sits between the lungs — what's it called?
Mediastinum: Central part of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum (from Medieval Latin: mediastinus, lit. 'midway';pl.: mediastina) is the central compartment of the thoracic cavity.
This theoretical physicist and science communicator bridged science and science fiction well enough to win a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for Arthur C. Clarke — who is he?
Michio Kaku: American theoretical physicist, futurist and author.

There's a large introduced population of this small carnivorous mammal in Hawaii, though its family — split into the Herpestinae and Mungotinae — is native to southern Europe, Africa, and Asia — what animal is it?

Mongoose: Family of mammals in Africa and Asia. The Herpestinae comprises 23 living species that are native to southern Europe, Africa and Asia, whereas the Mungotinae comprises 11 species native to Africa.
Found in cardiac and skeletal muscle and distantly related to hemoglobin, high levels of this oxygen-storing protein let diving whales and seals hold their breath longer — which protein?
A vitamer of vitamin B3 that the body can build from tryptophan, in large prescription doses it lowers LDL and raises "good" HDL cholesterol — what's this compound also called niacin?
Nicotinic acid: Organic compound and a form of vitamin B3.
Native to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this striped mammal looks like a zebra crossbred with a giraffe but is actually the giraffe's closest living relative — which animal?
Okapi: Species of mammal. Although the okapi has striped markings reminiscent of zebras, it is most closely related to the giraffe.

Produced in the hypothalamus and nicknamed for its role in love and social bonding, this peptide hormone also doubles as a pharmaceutical that speeds up childbirth by triggering uterine contractions — what is it?
Oxytocin: Peptide hormone and neuropeptide. Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
Nicknamed "javelina" or "skunk pig," this social New World mammal travels in herds called squadrons and counts true pigs as its closest living relatives — what pig-like ungulate is it?

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.
This beta blocker treats high blood pressure and performance anxiety alike, and can even shrink capillary hemangiomas in infants — what drug?
Propranolol: Beta blocker drug. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
First identified in the 1950s as a radio source, this extremely luminous galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy like the Milky Way thousands of times over — what is it?
Quasar: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) containing a supermassive black hole.
Often compared to the film in a camera, this innermost, light-sensitive layer of the eye sends signals along the optic nerve to the visual cortex — what is it?
Retina: Part of the eye. The retina (from Latin rete 'net'; pl. retinae or retinas) is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrograph images, this fecal-oral pathogen is the leading cause of diarrheal illness in infants worldwide — which pathogen?
Rotavirus: Specific genus of RNA viruses.
Found in every ocean but never in fresh water, most of these bivalves can swim in rapid bursts across the seafloor rather than staying put — which shellfish?
Scallop: Family of shellfish, many edible.
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.
A hygroscopic crystalline powder (formula NaNO2) and the most industrially important salt of its kind, this compound is most familiar to us cured into processed meats. What is it?
Sodium nitrite: Chemical compound. It is a white to slightly yellowish crystalline powder that is very soluble in water and is hygroscopic.
Derived from the Greek word for 'narrow,' this medical term describes the abnormal tightening of a blood vessel or other tubular structure — what is it?
Stenosis: Medical condition. Stenosis (from Ancient Greek στενός (stenós) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.

Allowing one neuron to send signals to a neighboring cell, this junction can be chemical or electrical, with coupled electrical types creating synchronized brain activity via gap junctions — what is it?
Synapse: Structure connecting neurons in the nervous system.
Also called lockjaw, this bacterial infection from Clostridium tetani starts spasms in the jaw before spreading body-wide, sometimes hard enough to fracture bone — what is it?
Tetanus: Bacterial infection characterized by muscle spasms.
Named from the Latin word for 'to ring,' this common condition causes people to perceive sounds — often ringing — that no one else can hear. What is it called?
Also called the jigger or chigoe flea, this burrowing parasite causes an infestation known as tungiasis and is often mistaken for an unrelated mite — which species?
Tunga penetrans: Species of flea. It is a parasitic insect found in most tropical and sub-tropical climates.
Released from the posterior pituitary when body fluids get too concentrated, this hormone helps kidneys reabsorb water and may also influence pair bonding — what is it?
Vasopressin: Mammalian hormone released from the pituitary gland.
Nicknamed the 'cock-of-the-woods,' this ground-dwelling grouse is the largest of all its kind, with males growing to nearly twice the size of females — which bird?
Western capercaillie: Species of bird. The bird shows extreme sexual dimorphism, with males nearly twice the size of females.
Nicknamed the ZZ plant or eternity plant, this glossy-leaved houseplant genus native to eastern Africa is prized for being nearly impossible to kill — name the genus?
Zamioculcas: Species of plant. Zamioculcas is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, containing the single species Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
Xenon is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for xenon is Xe. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Bismuth is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for bismuth is Bi. Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
